items.t: A single exclamation, three letters maximum, hand lettered near the person who made it.
Two words on a hand painted banner held between two of them.
One line of text written on a steamed window with a finger.
Text on a scrap of paper visible in frame, four words, in real handwriting rather than lettering.
One word repeated three times at decreasing size as somebody walks away.
A hand lettered arrow with two words next to it, pointing at the wrong thing.
Numbers only. A step number, a date or a price, nothing else.
One name, hand lettered, on a mug, a coat peg or a door.
A crossed out word and the correction above it, both hand written.
Text so small it reads as texture rather than words. No legible content.
One speech bubble with no words in it at all, just a full stop.
A short list of three items on a scrap, the third one absurd.
The words hand lettered in a curve following the shape of an object.
A shop or street sign in the background, three words, part of the world.
Two words on a t shirt, and nothing else anywhere in the image.
A whispered aside in a small bubble, five words, lower case.
One word painted enormous behind them, partly hidden by their bodies.
A single letter, three feet tall, that is all that remains of a longer sign.
A handwritten note stuck to something, six words, in a hurry.
Text spelled out in objects rather than lettering: magnets, cereal, chalk.
